established_findings.statement: Hallucination (fabricated or unsupported outputs) is a widely documented reliability problem for large language models that undermines trust in operational applications.
limitations: Most cited works are cross-domain surveys or simulated/specific-domain studies rather than NetOps field trials; they document the phenomenon but not uniform empirical rates in NetOps deployments.

established_findings.statement: Retrieval-augmented and evidence-grounded generation (RAG) designs can substantially reduce hallucination rates in operations-style question-answering and documentation tasks compared to naive retrieval approaches.
limitations: Evidence is from specific datasets and simulated evaluation protocols; generalization to all NetOps task types is not established by the supplied records.

established_findings.statement: Generate–validate–repair (tool-assisted or verifier-guided) architectures improve correctness for infrastructure-as-code (IaC) and other code-generation tasks in published studies.
limitations: Demonstrations are primarily in IaC, mathematics/program-verification, or general instruction-following benchmarks—not specifically on network-device configuration execution in operational NetOps testbeds.

established_findings.statement: LLMs can be applied to intent-driven network-configuration translation, but published work emphasizes fine-tuning, in-context learning, and continuous learning to improve accuracy rather than claiming turnkey deployment.
limitations: Reported evaluations focus on translation accuracy and model capability benchmarks rather than on executed, end-to-end network-change safety measurements.

established_findings.statement: Human-in-the-loop oversight is a pervasive recommendation for operational AI, but several works highlight structural limits (automation bias, liability framing) that constrain its effectiveness.
limitations: Analyses identify risks and behavioral limitations but vary in empirical scope and are not NetOps-only field trials.

established_findings.statement: Benchmarking efforts for LLM capabilities in NetOps/AIOps exist but remain nascent and heterogeneous (task scopes and metrics vary).
limitations: Existing benchmarks emphasize question/answer performance or capability evaluation rather than standardized, execution-level operational safety metrics.

unresolved_questions.statement: Do verifier-guided generate–validate–repair pipelines that improve IaC correctness (e.g., TerraFormer) transfer effectively to network-configuration generation to prevent unsafe or incorrect live configurations?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: cross-domain inference question supported by IaC and NetOps literature
limitations: No supplied record directly evaluates verifier-guided pipelines on network-device configuration execution; transferability is therefore an open empirical question.

unresolved_questions.statement: What fraction of LLM-generated network configurations would cause actionable misconfigurations when executed in network simulators or testbeds?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: measurement gap (absence noted among supplied records)
limitations: Supplied records include NetOps capability benchmarks and network-simulation surveys but do not report execution-based failure-rate measurements for LLM-generated configs.

unresolved_questions.statement: Which agentic or multi-agent orchestration patterns yield robust, auditable, and verifiable NetOps automation in practice?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: architectural / conceptual literature showing many proposals but limited validated patterns
limitations: Many agentic-system frameworks are conceptual or simulated; comparative, deployment-level evidence in NetOps contexts is not present in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is no supplied, standardized execution-based benchmark that measures operational correctness and safety of LLM-generated network configurations in network simulators/testbeds.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: gap identified by contrast between capability benchmarks and simulation infrastructure literature
limitations: This statement is based on the absence of such a benchmark among the supplied records; absence of evidence in this corpus does not prove no such benchmark exists outside the supplied set.

candidate_gaps.statement: NetOps-specific verifier/toolchain integrations analogous to verifier-guided IaC systems (e.g., TerraFormer) are underrepresented in the supplied literature.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: methodological gap (IaC verifier exists; NetOps-specific analogs not evident in supplied records)
limitations: NAssim and related works provide parsers/validators for device onboarding but do not demonstrate integrated LLM→verifier→repair pipelines for live network config execution in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is limited empirical understanding in the supplied records of how human-in-the-loop oversight performs under realistic NetOps operational constraints (time pressure, cognitive load).
limitations: Supplied analyses discuss structural limits and human roles but do not provide NetOps-specific controlled studies measuring oversight efficacy under operational stress.

candidate_gaps.statement: RAG pipelines in operations are vulnerable to adversarial poisoning that can induce hallucinations; defensive techniques are preliminary in the supplied corpus.
limitations: Adversarial examples and a single lightweight defense are demonstrated in SOC-style simulations; broader defensive evaluation for NetOps RAG pipelines is not present among the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Public, large-scale corpora of real network device configurations suitable for training/evaluating LLMs are not evident in the supplied record set.
limitations: Some curated and task-specific datasets (e.g., NetEval) exist, but the supplied records do not include extensive, execution-ready corpora of real/sanitized router configs for large-scale LLM training/evaluation.

excluded_claims: LLMs are production-ready to autonomously perform unsupervised, live network configuration changes without human oversight or formal verification (unsupported by supplied records).

This corpus demonstrates that verifier-guided RL approaches have been validated end-to-end for network-device configuration execution on live testbeds (no supplied record reports such an end-to-end NetOps execution evaluation).
Any single reviewed paper in the supplied set proves general superiority of one architectural pattern (e.g., agentic multi-agent frameworks) for safe NetOps automation across deployment contexts.
